# Reference: Real Cost at Typical Usage (Calibrated to a Measured Buyer Profile)

This dimension calibrates the abstract list-pricing in [`pricing-and-free-tier.md`](pricing-and-free-tier.md)
against one specific buyer's measured 13-day usage profile. The list price ($20/mo Pro
across most platforms) is not a complete cost picture — what matters for a buying
decision is what the same usage volume would cost at API rates and where the
subscription tier breaks. See [`citations.md`](../citations.md) for sources.

## The buyer's measured profile

Source: this buyer's instrumented usage of Claude Code on Pro $20/mo, sampled
from a SQLite statusline log (`claude_log_statuslines`), 2026-04-13 to 2026-04-25,
13 calendar days, 12 active days, 106 sessions, 14,764 statusline rows.

| Metric | Input + Output only | Cache-inclusive |
|---|---|---|
| Total tokens | 49.8M | 82.4M |
| Implied cache (read + creation) | — | 32.6M (+65%) |
| Weekly average | 26.8M | 44.4M |
| Daily average (calendar) | 3.83M | 6.34M |
| Daily average (active days) | 4.15M | 6.87M |
| Peak day (Sun 2026-04-19) | 22.2M | 29.8M |
| Per active minute | 25,323 | 41,928 |
| Per active hour | 630,179 | 1,043,422 |
| Total active time | 1,966 minutes (~33 hours) over 13 days | same |

Usage shape: weekend-heavy (Sat+Sun = 76% of total volume), weekday daytime
~0.9% of total volume on 1.2% of active time. One peak day = 36% of the
13-day total. Bursty agentic work, not steady throughput.

Both numbers matter, for different questions. **For dollar cost** at API rates,
the 49.8M input+output figure is the right anchor (cache reads bill at 10% of
fresh input, so 32.6M cache tokens add only ~$10 at Sonnet rates). **For
rate-limit / capacity**, the 82.4M cache-inclusive figure is the right anchor —
quota-bucketed plans (Cursor Pro $20 of API credits) and rate-limited plans
(Claude Code Pro/Max session caps) meter raw throughput, not effective-cost-
weighted throughput.

## 13-day API-rate cost projection (this buyer's profile)

The 49.8M input+output split between input and output is not separated in the
buyer's data — Claude Code's usage table reports the sum. Three input/output
split scenarios bracket the realistic range. Cache portion (32.6M) treated as
all cache reads (typical for sustained Claude Code sessions; the cache-creation
portion is unknown and would shift cost up by 1.25x–2x its fraction at write
rates — see Gaps).

All values rounded to nearest dollar.

| Model assumption | 90/10 input/output | 80/20 input/output | 70/30 input/output |
|---|---|---|---|
| All Sonnet 4.6 [41] | $219 | $279 | $338 |
| All Opus 4.7 [41] | $365 | $465 | $564 |
| 50/50 Sonnet+Opus mix | $292 | $372 | $451 |
| All GPT-5.4 [49] | $195 | $257 | $319 |
| All GPT-5.3-Codex [49] | $154 | $215 | $276 |
| All Gemini 3.1 Pro [50] | $156 | $206 | $256 |
| All Gemini 2.5 Pro [50] | $110 | $153 | $197 |
| All Cursor Composer 2 [47] | $41 | $51 | $61 |

**Worked example (90/10, all Sonnet 4.6):**
44.82M input × $3 + 4.98M output × $15 + 32.6M cache × $0.30
= $134.46 + $74.70 + $9.78 = $218.94. Rounded to $219.

**Worked example (80/20, 50/50 Opus+Sonnet mix):**
Half of (39.84M × $3 + 9.96M × $15 + 32.6M × $0.30) = ½ × $278.70 = $139.35
plus half of (39.84M × $5 + 9.96M × $25 + 32.6M × $0.50) = ½ × $464.50 = $232.25
= $371.60. Rounded to $372.

This buyer's measured volume scaled to a calendar month sits in roughly the

The MorphLLM analysis [54] independently characterizes Claude-Code-as-daily-agent

This buyer's projection sits in the lower-middle of that documented range.

## Subscription-tier coverage at this profile

Does the $20/mo Pro tier survive this buyer's measured volume? Two views.

### Throughput view (the rate-limit question)

The 82.4M cache-inclusive total is what platforms with raw-token quotas meter.

- **Claude Code Pro $20 [1][43]:** Anthropic does not publish absolute Pro caps;
  the only stated descriptor is "at least 5x usage per session vs free" [44].
  Empirically: a Pro subscriber quoted by *The Register* in March 2026 reported
  hitting weekly caps "every Monday" with reset on Saturday — "out of 30 days I
  get to use Claude 12" [46]. Anthropic's head of growth confirmed the platform
  is "hitting usage limits in Claude Code way faster than expected" and that
  fixing this is "the top priority for the team" [46]. The buyer's 82.4M
  throughput at 13-day pace = ~190M cache-inclusive tokens/month. There is no
  published Pro cap to compare against, but the empirical pattern (*Register*
  source, [56] author hitting Max weekly lockouts on $200) suggests this volume
  exceeds Pro and likely exceeds Max 5x.
- **Cursor Pro $20 [47]:** Hard cap. $20 of API credits at API rates buys
  ~225 Sonnet 4 requests per Cursor's own benchmark [48], or roughly 6.7M
  Sonnet input tokens at $3/M. The buyer's 49.8M non-cache + 32.6M cache
  scaled to one month = ~115M non-cache + ~75M cache. At Sonnet 4.6 rates,
  $20 covers ~3.5–6.5% of one month's usage volume — between 1 and 2 days of
  usage at this pace, then overage at API rates begins. Pro+ $60 ($70 credit)
  covers 12–22%. Ultra $200 ($400 credit) covers 70–90%, depending on split,
  and would still incur some overage. Confirmed by forum data: one user
  reported Auto + Opus consumption of ~$201 of API value against the $20 Pro
  plan [Cursor forum, cited via [48]].
- **Cursor Pro $20 with Composer 2 only [47]:** $20 covers ~10–14M of total
  Composer 2 usage. The buyer's scaled monthly volume in Composer 2 dollar-terms
  is ~$97–$145/mo. A Cursor-only stack at the buyer's volume needs Pro+ or
  Ultra even for the cheap Composer 2 model.
- **GitHub Copilot Pro $10 [12][51]:** 300 premium requests/month. Token-per-
  premium-request not published [51]. Pro+ users at 1,500 requests have
  reported burning the parallel weekly token cap at "as little as 20% of
  nominal quota" [51, derived from agent research and counter-discovery]. At
  this buyer's measured per-active-minute rate (25k+ non-cache tokens/min),
  300 requests would not survive a single intense agentic weekend session.
  GitHub's VP Joe Binder confirmed in announcing the 2026-04-20 signup pause
  that "a handful of requests can exceed the plan price" [58] — a direct
  admission that the $10 Pro plan was no longer compatible with agentic load.
- **Windsurf Pro $20 [21][52]:** Token-based quota since March 2026. Plan-
  specific numbers not published in the docs. Free models (SWE-1.6 family) do
  not count against quota, so a Windsurf-Pro user routing all work to SWE-1.6
  could absorb arbitrary volume — but BYOK or Sonnet/Opus usage burns the
  undisclosed token cap. The "unlimited" branding from earlier [21] is no
  longer accurate post-March 2026.
- **IBM Bob Pro $20 + $3 [26][29][53]:** 40 bobcoins/month. Token-per-bobcoin
  ratio is undocumented [53] — one community report puts a single MCP-driven
  Smalltalk analysis at ~40 bobcoins ($20 of consumption) for two hours of
  work. The buyer's profile (~33 active hours/13 days = ~76 hours/month) at
  comparable burn rate would consume ~1,520 bobcoins/month against a 40-coin
  Pro allocation — exceeding it by ~38x. Even Ultra ($230/mo, 500 coins)
  would not cover this profile if the MCP burn rate generalizes.

### Cost view (the dollar-equivalent question)

This view answers: "if the buyer ran identical traffic on each platform's
direct API, what would they pay?" It is the alternative-to-subscription cost.

Anchored on the 80/20 input/output, mixed Sonnet+Opus scenario as a realistic
midpoint:

| Platform / route | 13-day cost | Monthly extrapolated | Subscription that nominally covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anthropic API direct (50/50 Sonnet+Opus) | $372 | $858 | Max 20x ($200) covers if user manages session caps; Max 5x ($100) likely insufficient |
| Anthropic API direct (all Sonnet 4.6) | $279 | $644 | Max 20x ($200) is a 3.2x value buy |
| Anthropic API direct (all Opus 4.7) | $465 | $1,073 | Max 20x ($200) is a 5.4x value buy IF caps allow |
| Cursor API-rate billing (all Sonnet 4.6) | $279 | $644 | Ultra $200 ($400 credit) is closest, with overage |
| Cursor API-rate billing (all Composer 2) | $51 | $118 | Pro+ $60 ($70 credit) covers, Pro $20 does not |
| OpenAI API direct (GPT-5.4) | $257 | $593 | No comparable subscription on direct OpenAI. ChatGPT Plus $20 is a separate product |
| Google Gemini API direct (3.1 Pro) | $206 | $475 | Google AI Pro $19.99 has undisclosed Antigravity quota [19][50] |

The pattern: at this buyer's volume, **the $20/mo Pro tier provides
$100-$1,000+ of subscription-equivalent value compared to the same usage at
API rates** when the cap doesn't bind. Anthropic's apparent willingness to
limit (and briefly remove [5]) Claude Code on Pro is consistent with this
gap — Pro is heavily subsidized for heavy agentic users.

## Sensitivity to usage scaling

How does the answer change for users with 0.5x, 2x, and 4x this buyer's
measured volume? Linear scaling on the 80/20 mixed-model midpoint ($372 over
13 days, $858/mo):

| Multiplier | 13-day cost (mid) | Monthly cost (mid) | Realistic subscription fit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5x (light user) | $186 | $429 | Max 5x $100 likely covers. Cursor Pro+ $60 likely sufficient |
| 1.0x (this buyer) | $372 | $858 | Max 20x $200. Cursor Ultra $200 with overage |
| 2.0x (heavy weekend coder) | $744 | $1,716 | Max 20x $200 with usage management. Direct API may be cheaper above 2x |
| 4.0x (full-time agentic) | $1,488 | $3,432 | Direct API + budget caps strictly cheaper than any single subscription tier |

Above ~2x this buyer's volume, subscription pricing inverts: the all-you-can-eat
framing breaks because rate-limit lockouts make subscriptions unusable for
workdays at a time [46][56]. Direct API with explicit budget caps becomes
the controlled-cost path.

Below ~0.5x this buyer's volume, $20/mo subscriptions over-pay: a buyer doing
roughly 25M tokens/month would see $200-$400 of subscription-equivalent value
vs $20 paid — but at this load level any of the $20 plans would also work
without throttle, so the value gap is academic.

## The structural finding

The flat-rate $20/mo Pro tier is documented to be incompatible with sustained
agentic usage. Five concrete data points from primary sources, all dated
between 2025-06 and 2026-04:

1. **Cursor's June 2025 pricing apology** [10]: Pro changed from "500 requests"
   to "$20 of API credit" because the prior model could not absorb agentic
   token consumption. CEO public apology, refunds offered.
2. **Anthropic's 2026-03-26 peak-hour throttle** [46]: Active throttling was
   introduced for Claude Code with admission "people are hitting usage limits
   way faster than expected." Anthropic engineer estimated impact at "around 7
   percent of users" — a meaningful slice rather than an edge case.
3. **Anthropic's 2026-04-22 silent Claude Code removal from Pro** [5][57]:
   Documentation globally updated to remove Claude Code from $20 Pro plan
   coverage; reverted within 24 hours under public backlash. The fact this was
   attempted is direct evidence that Pro's economics were not viable for the
   actual usage pattern, not just a small test.
4. **GitHub Copilot's 2026-04-20 signup pause** [12][13][58]: New Pro and Pro+
   subscriptions paused with VP-level admission that "a handful of requests
   can exceed the plan price." Direct vendor statement that the $10/$39 plan
   prices could not sustain agentic compute demands.
5. **Max plan weekly lockouts** [56]: A $200/mo Max subscriber documents being
   locked out of Opus for several days mid-cycle (Oct 3 to Oct 6 lockout in
   the cited piece, with the user characterizing the limit as a "weekly limit"
   per the in-app message). The word "Max" implies ceiling; the actual ceiling
   is lower than what users expect to pay $200 for.

The published $20/mo price is accurate for the use case vendors designed it
for — non-agentic, intermittent assistance. It is not accurate for sustained
agentic coding sessions at the rate this buyer's profile demonstrates (25k+
tokens per active minute on weekend sessions). Until vendors transition to
explicitly token-metered billing (a structural shift discussed in [57]), the
gap between sticker price and real-cost value is large enough that buying
decisions made on sticker price alone will be wrong for any heavy-use buyer.

## Where the wall actually hits, calibrated to this buyer

A pragmatic decision framework for buyers with profiles within roughly 0.5x–2x
of this buyer's measured volume, accepting all the gaps below:

1. **Stay on Claude Code Pro $20 [1] only if** weekend usage shape lets the
   5-hour rolling window absorb the bursts. This buyer's measured 22.2M-token
   peak Sunday is large enough that Pro's weekly cap would likely have hit
   without active session management. Pro is workable here only because the
   buyer is implicitly throttling to fit the cap, not because the cap is
   generous.
2. **Move to Max 5x $100 [1][44]** if any single weekend session feels rushed
   under Pro. Max 5x is "5x more usage per session" [44]; for this buyer's
   ~12.5M-token peak Saturday, that would substantially relax the constraint.
3. **Move to Max 20x $200 [1][44]** if the user runs 2+ heavy weekend days
   per week. Max 20x covers this buyer's calendar-day average comfortably,
   but is still subject to weekly Sonnet-specific and cross-model caps [44]
   that have triggered multi-day lockouts (~3 days documented in [56]; the
   "weekly limit" framing implies up to 7 days is mechanically possible).
4. **Direct Anthropic API + budget caps [41][45]** above 2x this buyer's
   volume. The $2,000/day extra-usage cap [45] becomes the constraint instead
   of the subscription tier. This is also the route for predictable monthly
   costs: $400-$1,000/month is a budget the user controls, vs the
   subscription's "Max sometimes locks you out for a week."
5. **Cursor route makes financial sense only with Composer 2 dominance [47]**
   at this volume: the $0.50/$2.50/M Composer 2 rate puts monthly cost at
   ~$100-$150 against the Pro+ $60 ($70 credit) plan. Routing through Sonnet
   or Opus on Cursor at this volume requires Ultra $200 + overage and offers
   no cost advantage over going direct to Anthropic.
6. **Antigravity / Gemini Code Assist routes [17][19][50]** are theoretically
   the cheapest at sticker price (free or $19.99/mo), but the documented
   weekly-quota lockouts (3-10 days [19]) and undisclosed credit-to-token
   conversion [50] make them unreliable for sustained agentic use at this
   buyer's volume. Acceptable as a backup route during a primary-platform
   lockout, not as a primary route.

## Gaps and limitations

- **Input/output split is unknown.** The buyer's data sums input+output. The
  realistic range (90/10 to 70/30) yields cost estimates that vary by ~50%.
  The 80/20 midpoint is used as the modeling default; this is plausible for
  Claude Code [54] but not directly measured for this buyer.
- **Cache split (read vs write) is unknown.** The 32.6M cache figure combines
  cache_read and cache_creation. This analysis treats it all as cache reads
  ($0.30/M Sonnet, $0.50/M Opus). If 20% were cache writes at the 5-minute
  rate (1.25x base input), the cost projection rises by ~$3-$5 over 13 days —
  small in absolute terms but worth flagging. If the buyer's setup uses
  1-hour cache TTL (2x base input write), the impact is larger but still
  bounded; a worst-case all-cache-write scenario at Sonnet 4.6 rates is
  ~$200 over 13 days vs the $10 cache-read assumption.
- **Model mix is assumed, not measured.** The buyer's data does not separate
  Sonnet from Opus consumption. Claude Code on Pro defaults to Sonnet [2];
  the projections assume Sonnet-dominant unless flagged otherwise.
- **Linear monthly scaling is approximate.** Calendar month != 13-day window
  pattern. The buyer's measured period included two full weekends and one
  weekend day; a calendar month has 8-9 weekend days. Weekend-heavy usage
  shape implies actual monthly volume is closer to ~115M non-cache (the
  weekly average × 4.3) than the 13-day linear extrapolation (115M).
- **MorphLLM data points [54]** are practitioner-reported, not vendor-verified.
  The 90th-percentile spend "under $12/day" attributed to "Anthropic data" in
  the piece is not directly traceable to an Anthropic publication accessed in
  this research run; it should be treated as illustrative.
- **Vantage 50-turn $6 figure [55]** is for Opus 4.6 specifically; agentic
  session cost at Sonnet rates is roughly 1/1.67 = 60% of that figure.
- **Pro tier absolute caps remain undisclosed** [43][44]. The empirical
  practitioner reports of Pro caps [46] are single-user anecdotes; a
  systematic measurement of Pro's effective token ceiling at the time of
  this writing was not located in this research run.
- **Token-per-premium-request mappings undisclosed** for GitHub Copilot
  [51] and Windsurf [52]; Bobcoin-to-token ratio undisclosed [53]. These
  gaps are vendor-side opacity, not research-side gaps; they constrain any
  buyer-side cost projection regardless of methodology.
- **OpenAI Codex Business credit conversion not verified.** The discovery
  agent surfaced credit-per-million-token figures that imply Codex Business
  is significantly cheaper than direct API; this was not verified against a
  primary OpenAI source in this research run and is not used in the
  projections above.
